good_for: Disclosing and licensing a university invention
parent_org: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation
ideal_participant: Faculty, staff, and students with an invention or software developed using university resources
deadline_note: Disclosures accepted on a rolling basis via the Report Your Innovation page.
notes: Merged the map entries 'Office of Technology Management' and 'Disclosure & Licensing Information' (OTM section) into one resource; disclosure page is https://otm.illinois.edu/researchers-innovators/report-your-innovation. Office is clearly operating (2025 stats), but no 2026-dated evidence was found on the homepage, so status left Unknown. Student relevance depends on whether IP arose from university resources or employment.

name: Cancer Center at Illinois (CCIL)
description: An NCI-designated cancer research center at UIUC that funds engineering and data science approaches to cancer with seed grants and training programs. It has no startup program, but it connects researchers with Carle clinicians and translational research space.
good_for: Cancer technology research connections and seed grants for member teams
ideal_participant: Researchers and students working on cancer-related technology, diagnostics, or therapies
deadline_note: 2026 seed grant proposals were due March 11, 2026 (per search summary of CCIL seed grant info; not directly fetched).
notes: Status evidence: Homepage shows news dated October 8, 2026 and October 7, 2026. No entrepreneurship or commercialization program was found on the homepage. Grant programs (Seed, Bridge, Planning, High-Throughput Screening) are research grants that require Cancer Center membership. Student training includes a Cancer Education Undergraduate Certificate and graduate TiME Program. Publishes an 'Innovation Insider' newsletter.

name: Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology (IGB)
description: A campus genomics and life sciences institute with a bioeconomy and entrepreneurship arm, including a summer Early Innovator Program and a lecture series. Grad students and postdocs in related research can get commercialization training, mentors, and small proof-of-concept prizes.
good_for: Turning life science research into a startup
subcategory: Research institute with bioeconomy and entrepreneurship programs
ideal_participant: Graduate students, postdocs, and faculty doing biology or genomics research with commercial potential
deadline_note: Early Innovator Program runs 10 weeks starting the week of May 19 through end of July; page gives no year or application deadline.
cost_or_funding: Early Innovator Program top pitch winners receive up to $5,000 in proof-of-concept funding (per https://www.igb.illinois.edu/bioeconomy/igb-early-innovator-program)
notes: Status evidence: IGB homepage shows an October 2026 events calendar and Woese Prize nominations due November 15, 2026 (institute activity, not entrepreneurship-specific). Bioeconomy contact listed as Tracy Parish, Director of External Relations and Strategic Partnerships (tparish@illinois.edu). Early Innovator Program is open to University of Illinois grad students and postdocs whose work relates to an IGB theme. A search snippet from entrepreneurship.illinois.edu news referenced a 2026 Early Innovator pitch contest, not directly verified.

name: Carle Illinois College of Medicine (CI MED)
description: UIUC's engineering-based medical school, whose Office of Research and Innovation runs the Health Make-A-Thon, innovation seed grants, and medical device regulatory advising. Most funding and advising is reserved for CI MED students, though some events involve interdisciplinary student teams.
good_for: Health and medical device innovation
ideal_participant: CI MED students and faculty; other students interested in health tech via Make-A-Thon teams
deadline_note: Health Innovation Research Day was held April 3, 2026.
cost_or_funding: For CI MED students: Maker Coin of $10,000 per student across four categories; Research and Innovation Pathway Grants up to $3,000 per project (per https://medicine.illinois.edu/research-and-innovation)
notes: Status evidence: Research and Innovation page announces Health Innovation Research Day on April 3, 2026; CI MED 2026 graduation news published. Health Make-A-Thon and Health Maker Lab appear as separate map entries. Regulatory and development advising contact: yschleif@illinois.edu (CI MED faculty and students).

name: Corporate Innovation Centers
description: About 30 companies, including Fortune 500 firms, run innovation centers at Research Park to work with university faculty and hire student teams on real product and research projects. For students, these centers are the main source of paid internships and full-time job offers next to campus.
good_for: Working on industry R&D teams while in school
ideal_participant: Companies looking to open a campus innovation center. Students reach these centers through internships.
notes: Status evidence: The Research Park homepage shows 2026 news posts, including August 2026 items. The Corporate Innovation page currently markets the program to companies. This is a service for companies, which apply to become tenants. The page says more than 800 students work at Research Park year round. The figure of about 30 innovation centers comes from the student internship FAQ. Students reach these centers through the internships entry. Status evidence is park-wide activity, not a program-specific 2026 item.

name: Corporate Startup Intros
description: Research Park staff introduce startups, especially EnterpriseWorks companies, to corporations with innovation centers at the park, which can lead to partners, pilot customers, or investors. No official page describes how the service works.
good_for: Startups seeking corporate partners or pilot customers
ideal_participant: Founders of startups at EnterpriseWorks or Research Park looking for corporate partners. This is not a program students apply to directly.

The URL points to the team page because it lists Bailey Conrady, Associate Director of Community and Industry Partnerships (edenbur2@illinois.edu), the closest match for this service. The description is inferred from the ecosystem map label. Consider merging this into research-park-corporate-innovation-centers.

name: Gies College of Business
description: UIUC's business college, home of the Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship, which runs the iVenture Accelerator, EntreCorps consulting, and a student venture fund. Students get entrepreneurship coursework, including a minor offered jointly with Grainger, plus access to accelerator and investing programs.
good_for: Business-side entrepreneurship classes, accelerator, and student VC
ideal_participant: Students of any major interested in the business side of starting a company
notes: Status evidence: Gies Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship page says Orange and Blue Ventures is launching in Fall 2026. Umbrella college; entrepreneurship programs are run through the Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship (see ovael).

name: Hub for Brand Innovation and Advertising Technology (Brand Hub)
description: A College of Media unit, created by the Sandage Department of Advertising, the Siebel Center for Design, and Technology Services, that matched student teams with organizations on branding projects. Its website no longer loads, so it may be inactive.
good_for: Getting student help with startup branding and advertising
parent_org: Charles H. Sandage Department of Advertising, College of Media
ideal_participant: Startups needing branding or advertising help; advertising students seeking client projects
notes: Possibly defunct: brandhub.illinois.edu failed DNS lookup (ENOTFOUND) on 2026-10-13, and the newest Brand Hub items found in search date to roughly 2023 to 2024 (Brand Ambassador Program, events page listing 2021 to 2023 events). Contact email from cached site info only. Former official URL https://brandhub.illinois.edu/ did not resolve (DNS failure) on 2026-10-13.

name: Illinois Social Innovation
description: A campus-wide Gies initiative that trains students to tackle social and environmental problems through social entrepreneurship coursework, global programs, and hands-on impact projects. Participants can access mini-grants, seed capital eligibility, mentoring, and credit-bearing consulting projects.
good_for: Students building ventures or projects with a social impact mission
parent_org: Gies College of Business (Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship)
ideal_participant: UIUC students interested in social entrepreneurship and changemaking, from any major
notes: Program areas listed: Social Entrepreneurship Coursework, Global Entrepreneurship, Inclusive Entrepreneurship, Action Learning for Social Impact, Social Innovation Design Lab. Events and News sections were empty; no dated 2026 activity found. A newer OVAEL program list names Social Innovation Global Scholars rather than ISI itself, so ISI may now function as an umbrella brand. The School of Social Work also has an Illinois Social Innovation page.

name: Landuyt Center for Entrepreneurship
description: Grainger Engineering's entrepreneurship center, formerly the Technology Entrepreneur Center (TEC). It runs the Cozad New Venture Challenge, I-Corps, an IP clinic, startup advising, and entrepreneurship courses and certificates.
good_for: Taking entrepreneurship courses and entering campus startup competitions
ideal_participant: Any UIUC student exploring a startup idea or entrepreneurship coursework
cost_or_funding: Cozad New Venture Challenge has awarded $5M+ since 2000 (per landuyt.illinois.edu)
notes: Status evidence: landuyt.illinois.edu lists Oct 12, 2026 news naming seven Tech Startup Challenge finalists and Aug 27, 2026 news on expanding to Chicago. Renamed from Technology Entrepreneur Center (TEC). tec.illinois.edu still works and 301-redirects to https://landuyt.illinois.edu. Executive director Jed Taylor is also Grainger's Assistant Dean for Innovation and Entrepreneurship. The map also lists Grainger's Office of the Associate Dean for Innovation & Entrepreneurship. That role is now titled Assistant Dean for Innovation and Entrepreneurship, is held by the Landuyt Center director, and has no separate office page, so it is merged into this entry.

name: National Center for Supercomputing Applications (NCSA)
description: UIUC's supercomputing and data science center, which works with companies through an Industry Partner Program and runs student programs such as the SPIN undergraduate internship and the Fiddler Innovation Fellowship. Student founders can tap its computing resources, experts, and industry network.
good_for: Access to advanced computing, AI expertise, and industry partners
subcategory: Supercomputing center with industry and student programs
ideal_participant: Students and researchers building AI, data, or compute-heavy projects, and companies seeking research partnerships
notes: Status evidence: NCSA Industry Conference 2026 held October 13 to 14, 2026 (publish.illinois.edu/ncsa-industry-2026); NCSA news posts from May and August 2026. Industry partnerships contact listed as NCSA-Industry@mx.uillinois.edu; conference page lists industry@ncsa.illinois.edu. No startup-specific NCSA program was found; Industry Partner Program targets organizations. Student offerings include SPIN (spin.ncsa.illinois.edu).

name: Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation (OVCRI)
description: The campus office that oversees research and innovation at UIUC, including technology transfer, Research Park, EnterpriseWorks, and I-Corps, and that co-organizes Founders Week. Students and researchers can use it as a gateway to invention disclosure, startup handbooks, and entrepreneurship events.
good_for: Commercializing university research and finding campus startup support
ideal_participant: Graduate students and faculty with research they want to commercialize
notes: Status evidence: research.illinois.edu news covers Founders Week 2026 (Sept 30 to Oct 3) and the April 2026 Cozad New Venture Challenge. Owns and operates EnterpriseWorks (per Aug 21, 2026 Research Park article). Founders Week 2026 already took place Sept 30 to Oct 3, 2026.

name: Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship
description: Gies Business's entrepreneurship hub, now presented as the Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship. It runs the iVenture Accelerator, the EntreCORPS student consulting group, and student investing programs, and supports the entrepreneurship minor.
good_for: Joining a student startup accelerator or student VC fund
ideal_participant: UIUC students building a startup or wanting hands-on venture experience
cost_or_funding: iVenture Accelerator provides resources up to $20,000 (per giesbusiness.illinois.edu/origin-ventures-office-of-entrepreneurship)
notes: Status evidence: Official page says Orange and Blue Ventures is launching in Fall 2026. Naming: the Origin Ventures Academy for Entrepreneurial Leadership (OVAEL, est. 2004 as the Academy for Entrepreneurial Leadership, renamed 2018) was expanded into the Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship, announced April 21, 2025. The announcement frames it as an expansion, not an explicit rename, but the current official page uses only the Office name and does not mention OVAEL. The old giesgroups.illinois.edu/ovael page returned no meaningful content. No email on the page; phone 217-300-7327.

name: Research Park at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
description: A university technology park in Champaign with 100+ companies, the EnterpriseWorks incubator, and entrepreneurs-in-residence. Students can find paid internships at corporate and startup tenants, and founders can get incubation and startup support.
good_for: Finding tech internships and startup incubation near campus
parent_org: Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation
ideal_participant: Students seeking internships and founders looking for incubation and corporate connections
notes: Status evidence: Homepage lists 2026 news items including Sep 23 podcast and Aug 21 'named a top incubator and accelerator'. Homepage reports 350+ startups nurtured. AgTech Summit and Founders Week listed without dates.

name: Research Park Recruitment Services
description: Research Park helps its tenant companies recruit UIUC students through a job board, career fair, and campus recruiting events. The service is for companies, so students benefit through the postings and employer events.
good_for: Companies hiring UIUC student talent
subcategory: Talent recruiting support for tenant companies
ideal_participant: Research Park and EnterpriseWorks companies, including student-founded startups at EnterpriseWorks, that need to hire. Students looking for jobs should use the internships entry.
notes: No dedicated page exists. The Affiliation Benefits page lists 'recruiting assistance' as a tenant benefit. The team page lists Bryan Goode, Talent Manager (bdgoode@illinois.edu), for workforce development and recruitment. Consider merging with research-park-workforce-development.

name: The Grainger College of Engineering
description: UIUC's engineering college, which houses the Landuyt Center and backs student startup programs such as the Cozad New Venture Challenge and the Grainger Engineering Tech Startup Challenge. Students get entrepreneurship courses, certificates, an engineering entrepreneurship dual degree, and pitch opportunities.
good_for: Finding engineering entrepreneurship courses, degrees, and startup competitions
ideal_participant: Engineering students interested in starting a company or studying entrepreneurship
cost_or_funding: Grainger Engineering Tech Startup Challenge offers a prize pool of over $200,000 (per grainger.illinois.edu/academics/entrepreneurship)
notes: Status evidence: Grainger entrepreneurship page shows Aug 27, 2026 news on Landuyt Center expanding to Chicago and an Oct 13, 2026 Q&A story. Umbrella college; the entrepreneurship programs themselves are mostly run by the Landuyt Center. Map links the general college site; the entrepreneurship page is more useful for founders. The university research calendar lists the Tech Startup Challenge at the Chicago Venture Summit on Oct 20, 2026.

name: Champaign County Economic Development Corporation
tagline: County economic development group that hosts free small business advising
description: Champaign County's economic development organization, home to the local Small Business Development Center. Founders who live in the US can request free, confidential advising on starting or growing a business and learn about local funding programs.
what_it_is: A public and private economic development organization for Champaign County that houses the local Illinois Small Business Development Center (SBDC), which gives free, confidential one on one business advising.
who_should_apply: Student founders starting or running a business in the Champaign County area who are US citizens or legal residents; no stage requirement.
choose_this_if: You want free, confidential advice from a local business advisor on starting or growing a company in Champaign County.
good_for: Free small business advising and local business funding programs
ideal_participant: Student founders forming a local business in Champaign County
apply_steps: Submit the Request No-Cost Advising form on the SBDC site | Meet an advisor by appointment
deadline_note: SBDC advising requests are accepted at any time; meetings are by appointment only (cusbdc.org). City small business grant rounds have their own windows not checked here.
cost_or_funding: SBDC advising is free per https://cusbdc.org/
notes: Status evidence: cusbdc.org shows a live advising request form and a booking calendar for existing clients; EDC homepage lists the SBDC as no-cost and confidential. CCEDC also named a new SBDC director in May 2026 per search results. Office at 1817 S. Neil St, Suite 100, Champaign. Also runs Made in Champaign County and C-U AgTech Week, and is involved in the iFAB biomanufacturing Tech Hub. The EDC site's own news feed was last updated July 2024. Footer email domain is .com while staff emails use .org.

name: Chicago Quantum Exchange (CQE)
tagline: Midwest quantum science consortium with a paid summer undergrad research fellowship
description: A Midwest quantum consortium of universities, labs, and companies. Undergrads can apply for its Open Quantum Initiative fellowship, a 10 week summer research placement with a $7,000 stipend, housing, and travel, and browse quantum jobs and events.
what_it_is: A consortium of universities including Illinois, national labs, and companies based at the University of Chicago that runs quantum education programs, job listings, and the Open Quantum Initiative (OQI) summer research fellowship for undergraduates.
who_should_apply: Undergrads at any US college who have finished freshman year with at least 4 STEM courses can apply for the OQI fellowship; no research experience needed, and rising sophomores and juniors get preference.
choose_this_if: You want a paid summer of hands-on quantum research at a lab such as Argonne, Fermilab, UChicago, or UIUC.
good_for: Quantum careers, internships, and research fellowships
parent_org: University of Chicago (Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering)
ideal_participant: Students and founders in quantum science and engineering
apply_steps: Complete the online application with one reference letter | Write two 300 to 500 word statements on your quantum interests and a challenge you overcame | Upload a transcript
deadline_note: OQI fellowship 2026 cycle closed February 10, 2026 (HQAN OQI page); the CQE fellowship page says applications are closed for 2026 and no 2027 date is posted yet. Deadlines have fallen in early February.
cost_or_funding: OQI fellows receive a $7,000 stipend, on-campus housing, and travel (2026 terms per CQE fellowship page)
notes: Status evidence: CQE fellowship page lists 2026 program dates at each host site (UIUC: May 26 to July 31, 2026) and an info session sign up; CQE homepage has October 2026 news. UIUC is a placement site for OQI fellows and IQUIST helped fund the Summer 2024 OQI program. Q-Ready (free, for students in IL, WI, IN) seen only in search snippets, not verified on an official page. UIUC member status not clearly labeled on homepage.

name: Discovery Partners Institute (DPI)
tagline: U of I System's Chicago tech institute, home of the paid City Scholars internship
description: The U of I System's Chicago institute for AI research and industry partnerships. UIUC juniors and seniors in CS, CE, or EE can apply to City Scholars, a semester in Chicago with a part-time paid internship plus classes.
what_it_is: The University of Illinois System's Chicago institute that links UIUC research with Chicago industry on AI; UIUC students mainly reach it through Grainger's City Scholars program, a part-time paid internship while taking classes in Chicago for a semester.
who_should_apply: UIUC undergrads with junior standing in CS, CS + X, computer engineering, or electrical engineering who have taken or are taking the required course (3.2 GPA recommended).
choose_this_if: You want to spend a semester in Chicago working at a tech company while taking UIUC classes.
good_for: Spending a semester working in Chicago tech
subcategory: University of Illinois System Chicago institute
ideal_participant: Junior or senior CS, CE, CS+X, or EE students wanting Chicago tech experience
apply_steps: Check eligibility and the prerequisite course for your major | Prepare a resume and a statement of interest of up to 200 words | Submit the online application during the window
deadline_note: City Scholars Spring 2027 applications ran August 24 to September 13, 2026; rankings due November 8, 2026; program runs January 19 to May 5, 2027 (City Scholars application page). No Fall 2027 window posted yet.
notes: Status evidence: City Scholars application page shows a Spring 2027 cohort running January 19 to May 5, 2027; DPI homepage features a September 2026 op-ed. DPI's other talent programs target K-12 and community college students. City Scholars is run by Grainger and hosted at DPI; it may deserve its own directory entry. No email listed; contact via https://dpi.illinois.edu/about/contact.

name: Duality Quantum Accelerator
tagline: Quantum startup accelerator, now run as the quantum track of Alchemist Chicago
description: A quantum startup accelerator now run inside Alchemist Chicago. Teams that advance from a one week Chicago bootcamp get a $50K investment (most give about 4% equity), Duality mentoring, and lab space for quantum hardware companies.
what_it_is: A Chicago accelerator for quantum technology startups, founded by UChicago's Polsky Center and the Chicago Quantum Exchange with UIUC as a founding partner, that now runs inside the Alchemist Chicago deep tech accelerator.
who_should_apply: Pre-seed or seed quantum startups with at least two technical co-founders who can attend in person in Chicago and San Francisco; student founders qualify only with a formed team at that stage.
choose_this_if: You are building a quantum hardware or software startup and want investment, lab space, and mentors in Chicago.
good_for: Launching a quantum hardware or software startup
parent_org: Polsky Center (UChicago) and Chicago Quantum Exchange
ideal_participant: Founders of early-stage quantum technology startups
apply_steps: Optionally attend an Alchemist Chicago info session | Submit the application through Apply Now on the Alchemist Chicago page
deadline_note: Latest round (2027 cohort) opened July 13, 2026 and closed in August 2026; the Alchemist Chicago page says August 20, 2026 while the Duality about page says August 14, 2026. Program started October 19, 2026. Next round not posted; past rounds opened in July.
